title: 得有主体性，才配投入一段感情

timeline.summary: A viewer asks how to preserve selfhood while seriously investing in a relationship.
Mikey defines the self as one's underlying personhood and uses harsh insults to say that investment without subjectivity becomes servile dependence.
He says subjectivity means retaining the choice to invest or not; he speculates that investment may support a longer relationship while noninvestment may remain casual.
He concludes that subjectivity is a root of attraction.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He frames subjectivity as retaining one's own agency and the ability to choose whether and how deeply to invest in a relationship.
claims.conditions: Agency does not mean disregard for a partner; mutual care, consent and responsibility remain necessary.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He suggests that emotional investment can support a longer relationship, while noninvestment may leave it casual.
claims.conditions: A broad, unsupported generalization; relationship duration depends on both people and many other conditions.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He calls subjectivity a root of attraction.
claims.conditions: A conceptual claim from this excerpt, not demonstrated causal evidence.
